structure.title: Athens and the wood
structure.text: The city's marriage rules give way to a forest where desires and identities can be altered.

structure.title: Returning to performance
structure.text: Private confusion enters public celebration and amateur theatre. Lovers, fairies, and craftsmen cross one another's plots.

context.title: Three kinds of authority
context.text: Fathers and rulers command, fairies interfere, and actors try to direct what an audience imagines. Each group believes it can arrange other people's experience.

context.title: Performance
context.text: The craftsmen worry that spectators will mistake an acted danger for a real one. Their solutions are funny, but touch the larger play's interest in illusion.
context.takeaway: Bad theatre can expose how theatre works.

notice.text: Listen to confident explanations of newly changed desires.
notice.why: Sincerity does not mean the speaker understands the cause.

notice.text: Track sleep, waking, and the moon.
notice.why: They offer competing accounts of experiences nobody fully controls.

opening: Hermia must marry the man her father chooses or face a punishment she cannot accept. She runs into the woods with the man she loves, followed by two people whose desires make the situation worse. The fairies living there have a marriage dispute of their own and access to something human lovers lack: a way to change whom someone wants. By morning, love will have produced magnificent declarations, atrocious behaviour, and very little evidence that anyone understands what has happened to them.
